title: Ob spring flow width trend limits depended on block length in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested the width between the 25% and 75% dates of April-July discharge at Ob, Lena and Yenisey in 31 common certified years from 1980 to 2011, excluding 2000. Width trends were +1.228, +0.418 and +0.535 days per decade. Joint five-year residual block resampling gave adjusted Ob limits of +0.003 to +2.517. An added 100,000-draw check gave -0.002 to +2.539. Three- and seven-year block limits also included zero. A 1990 start reduced the Ob trend to +0.143. All planned adjusted Lena and Yenisey limits included zero. The records do not give stable evidence for a common increase in central-half spring flow width. Fixed windows, short partly gapped records, regulation and conditional block uncertainty limit the result. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and an independent numerical audit are included. Raw data and annual derived tables stay external.

display.caption: The central half of April-July flow had positive width trend estimates at three gauges. Adjusted block limits were uncertain. The near-zero Ob lower limit changed sign in an added simulation check.
